name: Prepare servicer reports for funders
summary: The company sells pools of leases to bank-sponsored commercial paper conduits but keeps collecting the payments as servicer, so every month it must tell each conduit what happened to its pool. A securitisation analyst extracts the pool data, reconciles collections to the collection account, processes payouts, restructures and defaults, calculates repurchases, delinquency and loss ratios, tests the performance triggers and works out the reserve and distributions. A second analyst checks the report, the treasurer signs the servicer certificate and releases the remittance, and the conduit reviews it. Spreadsheet models, data fixes, collection breaks and waiting for the month-end close make the work slow and error-prone.

baseline.org_archetype: A privately owned Canadian independent equipment lessor funding about 65% of its $1.5 billion of receivables through three bank-sponsored ABCP conduits.
baseline.notes: One report per funding facility per month, about four a month (one conduit reports two series separately). Annual servicer reviews by funders are outside this case.

trigger: The month ends and the month-end pool data are loaded; collections, pool change notices and closed balances arrive during the case.
end_state: The signed servicer report and data file are accepted by the conduit, the remittance or reserve transfer is released and the pool tracker is updated.

volume.seasonality: Same every month; quarter-ends add funder questions and 2020 added deferral reporting.

evidence.note: Organisation file range; three conduits, one with two series reported separately. Canadian conduit transactions backed by equipment leases are documented.

Loaded cost from the organisation file (2019-2022 wage times 1.35). Servicer reports, funder questions and annual servicer reviews take about 0.85 of the three analysts' time; pool sales and buyouts are separate processes.
Loaded cost from the organisation file (2019-2022 wage times 1.35). Reviews and signs four reports a month and handles trigger issues with sponsors.
Loaded cost from the organisation file (2019-2022 wage times 1.35). Fixes failed or wrong pool extracts a few times a month.

systems.name: Data warehouse and business intelligence reports
Lease management system (contracts, schedules, billing, tax codes, asset records, servicing)
Spreadsheet models (pool cuts, borrowing base, covenants, budget, tax workpapers)
Bank cash management portal for pre-authorised debit files, EFT payments and wires
General ledger and accounts payable (mid-market ERP)
Document imaging and contract file store

steps.name: Run the month-end batch and load pool data
steps.description: After the last business day of the month the lease system runs its month-end processing and the overnight load refreshes the data warehouse with contract balances, payments, delinquency status and the pool code of every securitised contract.

evidence.note: Author estimate of the common month-end batch.

steps.name: Extract the pool data and load the servicer report model
steps.description: The securitisation analyst runs the warehouse query for this conduit's pools and pastes the contract-level results into the servicer report workbook: opening and closing balances, scheduled and received payments, prepayments, delinquency status, defaults, charge-offs, recoveries and modifications. Pool sales take priority in the first days of the month, so reports queue.

error.defect_description: Wrong cut-off date or a pool code filter that drops contracts.

next.condition: load failed or pool codes missing

evidence.note: Report content follows the sources; times and failure rate are author estimates.

steps.name: Fix a failed or incomplete pool extract
steps.description: A data and business intelligence developer finds why the extract is short or wrong, for example a failed overnight load, contracts missing their pool code after a restructure or a changed status code, fixes the data or the query and reruns it.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Reconcile pool collections to the collection account
steps.description: The analyst ties the month's cash applied to this conduit's contracts (from cash application) to the deposits and transfers on the collection account bank statement and to the amounts already remitted or held for the conduit, and lists any differences.

control.basis: Servicing agreement and internal control: collections reported to the conduit reconcile to the collection account

evidence.note: Collections are earmarked to the pool where the lease is funded; break rate is an author estimate.

steps.name: Investigate collection breaks with cash application
steps.description: The analyst emails the cash application team about misapplied payments, debits returned after the cut-off, unidentified receipts and payouts posted to the wrong contract, and waits for corrections or explanations.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Review the month's pool change notices
steps.description: The analyst works through the notices of payouts, assumptions, restructures and deferrals, defaults and write-offs on securitised contracts, checks each against the lease system and flags contracts whose change breaks the eligibility criteria or the servicing standards.

error.defect_description: A modified contract is missed and stays in the pool.

evidence.note: Restructured and seriously delinquent leases are typical exclusions; the repurchase frequency is an author estimate.

steps.name: Calculate repurchases of ineligible or modified contracts
steps.description: For contracts that were restructured, assumed or found ineligible, the analyst calculates the repurchase price (the discounted balance plus arrears) and, where the facility allows, picks eligible unsold contracts to substitute.

error.defect_description: Repurchase price uses the wrong discount rate.

control.basis: Receivables purchase agreement: seller repurchases receivables that breach eligibility representations

evidence.note: Repurchase mechanics are author estimates of typical facility terms.

steps.name: Approve the repurchase and substitution list
steps.description: The treasurer checks the repurchase amounts and substitutes against the facility terms and the cash forecast and approves them, because repurchases use the company's cash or bank line.

control.basis: Treasury authority for repurchases and substitutions

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Receive the conduit's funding cost and fee statement
steps.description: The sponsor bank's administrator sends the month's commercial paper cost, program and liquidity fees for this facility, which the waterfall needs. It usually arrives while the reconciliation is under way.

evidence.note: Author estimate; it runs in parallel with the reconciliation steps.

steps.name: Calculate the pool balance and performance ratios
steps.description: The analyst calculates the discounted pool balance at the facility's discount rate, the pool factor, delinquency by bucket (one to four payments late), the monthly default ratio, cumulative net losses after recoveries and the prepayment rate, and compares them with last month.

error.defect_description: Formula or range error in the workbook.

evidence.note: Items follow the servicer statement in the prospectus; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Test the triggers and calculate the reserve and distributions
steps.description: The analyst compares the delinquency, default and loss ratios with the facility's trigger levels, works out the required cash reserve and overcollateralization, and runs the waterfall: conduit interest and fees, principal paydown, servicing fee and any excess spread released to the company.

error.defect_description: Wrong trigger level or reserve percentage used.

control.basis: Securitisation facility terms: performance triggers, cash reserve and overcollateralization requirements

next.condition: a trigger is breached or close

evidence.note: Seller credit enhancement through excess spread, overcollateralization and reserves; breach frequency is an author estimate (higher in 2020).

steps.name: Escalate a trigger breach with the sponsor
steps.description: The treasurer reviews the breach or near-miss with the CFO, calls the sponsor bank, agrees whether excess spread is trapped, the reserve topped up, the pool topped up with new contracts or a waiver requested, and has the analyst reflect the result in the report.

evidence.note: Author estimate; during the 2020 deferral period conduits granted relief on deferred contracts.

steps.name: Tie the pool to the closed month ledger
steps.description: When accounting finishes the month-end securitisation reconciliation, the analyst compares the pool balances, collections and reserve with the closed securitisation subledger and liability balances, and explains or fixes differences.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting: securitisation balances reported to funders agree to the ledger (securitised leases stay on balance sheet)

evidence.note: Securitised leases stay on balance sheet with a securitisation liability; the wait follows the month-end close of about eight business days.

steps.name: Prepare the servicer report and data file
steps.description: The analyst fills the conduit's report template with collections, pool balances, delinquencies, defaults, recoveries, repurchases, trigger tests, reserve and distributions, and exports the contract-level data file in the conduit's layout.

error.defect_description: Figures pasted into the wrong template cells or period.

evidence.note: Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Second analyst checks the report
steps.description: Another securitisation analyst re-checks the key figures against the model and the reconciliations: collections tie-out, ratios, trigger levels, reserve and the distribution amounts, and returns errors.

control.basis: Treasury procedure: maker-checker review of funder reports

evidence.note: Author estimate of common practice.

steps.name: Treasurer reviews and signs the servicer certificate
steps.description: The treasurer reviews the report, the trigger results, repurchases and the remittance amount, and signs the servicer's officer certificate that the report is accurate and the servicer has met its obligations.

control.basis: Servicing agreement: officer's certificate with each monthly report

evidence.note: Author estimate of typical servicing agreement terms.

steps.name: Submit the report and data file to the conduit
steps.description: The analyst uploads the signed report, certificate and data file to the conduit administrator's portal or sends them by secure email to the sponsor's securitisation team before the reporting date.

evidence.note: Conduits must publish monthly disclosure within 50 days of month-end, so sellers report well before that.

steps.name: Set up the monthly remittance or reserve transfer
steps.description: The analyst enters in the bank portal the transfer the waterfall requires: collections due to the conduit, a reserve top-up, or the receipt of released excess spread, with the report attached for approval.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Release the remittance
steps.description: The treasurer checks the pending payment against the signed report and releases it in the bank portal; no single person can both set up and release a funder payment.

control.basis: Treasury payment control: dual authorisation of wires

evidence.note: Author estimate of common practice.

steps.name: Conduit administrator reviews the report
steps.description: The sponsor's team checks the report against the data file and its own records, recalculates the triggers and the distribution and may send questions.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Answer conduit questions or correct the report
steps.description: The analyst explains movements such as a jump in deferrals or a large default, sends supporting contract detail and, where an error is found, corrects and resubmits the report.

evidence.note: Shares are author estimates.

steps.name: File the report and update the pool performance tracker
steps.description: The analyst files the final report and certificate, adds the month's delinquency, default, loss and prepayment figures to the pool tracker used for pricing the next pool sale and for management reporting, and sends a short summary to the treasurer.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

exceptions.name: Failed or incomplete pool extract
exceptions.description: The warehouse load failed or contracts lack pool codes; a data developer fixes the extract.

exceptions.name: Collection breaks
exceptions.description: Cash applied to pool contracts does not tie to the collection account and the analyst chases cash application.

exceptions.name: Repurchases or substitutions
exceptions.description: Restructured, assumed or ineligible contracts are repurchased or substituted with treasurer approval.

exceptions.name: Trigger breach or near-miss
exceptions.description: A delinquency, default or loss ratio breaches or nears its trigger; the treasurer agrees the response with the sponsor.

exceptions.name: Ledger difference
exceptions.description: Pool balances do not tie to the closed securitisation subledger and figures are recalculated.

exceptions.name: Conduit questions
exceptions.description: The sponsor asks about movements or finds an error; the analyst answers or resubmits.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from month-end to the conduit accepting the report
benchmarks.population: Canadian independent equipment lessor reporting to bank-sponsored ABCP conduits, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Author estimate: the final tie-out follows the month-end close (about 11 calendar days in efc-close-the-month) and reports reach sponsors in the third week so conduits can publish their monthly disclosure within 50 days.

benchmarks.population: Canadian ABCP conduits relying on the NI 45-106 ABCP exemption

benchmarks.unit: cash proceeds divided by securitised lease and loan balances

evidence.note: $962.7 million divided by $1,071.3 million.

pain_points.description: Reports are built in spreadsheet models from warehouse extracts, so formula, range and template errors are common and need a second analyst to catch.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

pain_points.description: Collections often do not tie to the collection account on the first pass because of misapplied and returned payments around the cut-off.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

pain_points.description: Pool change notices arrive by email from several teams and modified contracts are easy to miss, which can lead to late repurchases.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

pain_points.description: The final tie-out waits for the month-end close, compressing the time left before the reporting date.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

sources.title: A primer on the Canadian asset-backed commercial paper market
sources.supports: Most Canadian bank-sponsored conduits are multi-seller programs buying third-party assets including equipment leases; sellers give first-loss enhancement through excess spread, overcollateralization and cash reserves; conduits relying on the ABCP exemption publish a Form 45-106F8 monthly disclosure report on asset pools and their performance no later than 50 days after month-end.

sources.title: Charter Equipment Lease 1998-1 LLC prospectus (Form 424B1)
sources.supports: The servicer prepares a statement each period with fees, outstanding balances, pool factor, discounted lease balance, unreimbursed servicer advances, recoveries on defaulted leases and leases one to four payments delinquent, and delivers a monthly servicer report to the rating agencies; defaulted leases are those more than 120 days delinquent or charged off; collections are earmarked to the pool where the lease is funded.

sources.title: DBRS Morningstar updates Pure Grove Funding transaction 102
sources.supports: A Canadian ABCP conduit transaction backed by fixed-rate equipment leases on commercial trucks, with a $500 million program limit and several conduit lenders, rated under the Canadian equipment finance securitization methodology.

sources.title: Eligible lease receivables (definitions from credit agreements)
sources.supports: Sample definitions exclude leases more than 61 days (or 120 days) past due, in default, not subject to a first priority perfected security interest, restructured for credit reasons, or above lessee concentration limits.

sources.title: CWB Financial Group Annual Report 2021, note 8: securitization
sources.supports: Securitized equipment leases and loans of $1.07 billion in 2021 for cash proceeds of $963 million do not qualify for derecognition, so a securitization liability is recognised.

sources.title: Financial/Securitization Analyst (job posting)
sources.supports: A Toronto non-bank lender with equipment leasing: prepares tranches for funders, pays funders on time, produces monthly compliance reports, sends regular reports to funders, supports funder audits and makes borrowing requests; Excel and Great Plains.

assumptions: One case is one facility's monthly report; four a month (three conduits, one reporting two series).

Collections data, pool change notices, the new pool from the latest sale and closed balances are listed as triggers with a share of zero because they arrive inside the case; the month-end pool data start it.
The existing close-the-month workflow does not list closed_month_balances as an output to this process, although the organisation file does; this file follows the organisation file.
Facility terms (trigger levels, reserve rules, repurchase obligations, reporting dates) are private; the items listed are typical of rated equipment securitisations and are author estimates.
The second-analyst check uses another securitisation analyst; with three analysts this is feasible but slips in busy months.
External steps have no touch time; the sponsor's statement and review are in wait_before_min.
Loaded costs are the organisation file's (2019-2022 wage times 1.35).
